frontend-infra-book.eyebrow: A field guide for frontend builders
frontend-infra-book.summary: An open-source guide to frontend system design, infrastructure, and engineering decisions.

chapters.title: Why this book exists
chapters.body: While preparing for architectural frontend interviews, I found many system-design resources focused on backend problems. I brought together lessons from my career, conversations, and mock interviews to create a frontend-focused guide.

chapters.title: Plan the system
chapters.body: Explore product requirements, technical requirements, backend integration, security, and DevOps. The chapters offer questions and tradeoffs to consider when planning a frontend system.

chapters.title: Build shared foundations
chapters.body: The design-system chapter covers common components, typography, spacing, forms, loading states, and other foundations that help teams build consistently.

chapters.title: Keep it responsive
chapters.body: The performance chapter explores loading speed, bundle size, mobile considerations, and the tradeoffs involved in choosing tools and rendering strategies.

picklejs.eyebrow: A little pickle with a practical job
picklejs.summary: An open-source integration-testing library developed at HOVER to make scenarios easier to write and maintain.

chapters.title: The problem
chapters.body: Integration tests were accumulating repetitive setup and hard-to-follow code. UI changes could also force repeated selector updates.

chapters.title: Readable steps
chapters.body: PickleJS grew from Cypress and Cucumber experiments: reusable English-like steps, shared patterns, and selectors collected in JSON.

chapters.title: Built to be extended
chapters.body: The library grew into modular tools that teams could adapt to their own needs. HOVER released it as its first open-source project.

nyc-leetcode-squad.summary: A New York community that brings people together to practice algorithms, prepare for coding interviews, and help one another learn.

chapters.title: It started with a post
chapters.body: I wanted a more social way to practice LeetCode and stay accountable. After posting on Blind, I organized a first gathering that brought together 26 people, from students to experienced engineers.

chapters.title: Learn in good company
chapters.body: The group combines larger meetups with small study pods, mentorship, and interview practice. Members share approaches to problems and help each other build confidence.

chapters.title: Find your people
chapters.body: The community welcomes different experience levels, with in-person gatherings and a Discord space for virtual practice and organizing local pods.

easter-creatures.summary: A Miami Easter-egg experiment by Toli and Asya, connecting children’s creature drawings with a neighborhood treasure hunt and an NFT collection.

chapters.title: A weekend experiment
chapters.body: The idea began the morning before Easter: hide eggs around Miami with something unexpected inside. Toli and Asya set themselves the challenge of bringing it to life in 24 hours.

chapters.title: Draw, hide, discover
chapters.body: Children supplied the creature drawings. The team made them into NFTs, placed printed QR codes inside eggs, and hid the eggs around Miami, with many in Wynwood.

chapters.title: More than an egg hunt
chapters.body: The project became a way to meet neighbors and invite people into art and technology. Its story shares the practical surprises, last-minute printing scramble, and encouragement they found along the way.
